400.description: Bad Request - Invalid query parameters (e.g., malformed cursor, invalid workspaceId format, search query too long, a compound sort, or a cursor minted under a different sort)

post.description: Creates and starts a new simulation based on the specified configuration. The simulation begins in `validating` status, or in `provisioning` for simulations that skip that status, then progresses to `running`. Poll the GET endpoint to monitor progress. `checkpointing` is accepted but not yet supported.

400.description: Bad Request; no simulation is created. Code VALIDATION_ERROR when the simulation parameters are invalid. Code LAUNCH_CONFIG_INVALID when the configuration could not be prepared for the simulator: the message says why, and resubmitting it unchanged fails again.

402.description: Payment Required - the platform's credit balance is exhausted. Add credits before launching simulations.

409.description: Conflict; no simulation is created. Code CONFLICT when a simulation with this name already exists in the workspace: choose another name. Code MAPPING_FILE_DELETED_REFERENCE when the Chakra mapping file attached to the configuration has been deleted: the message names the file. Detach it, or attach another mapping file, and create the simulation again.

422.description: No simulation is created. Code UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY when the configuration is not validated: it must have status `validated` before starting a simulation. Code LAUNCH_REJECTED when the simulator rejected the configuration: resubmitting it unchanged fails again.

503.description: Service Unavailable - the simulation service could not start the simulation. No simulation is created, so the request can be retried.

post.description: Compares two to four simulations and returns aligned summaries, per-metric deltas and a diff context. The result is returned inline as JSON rather than as a presigned download envelope.

get.summary: Get computed summary data for simulation results
get.description: Computes or retrieves cached summary statistics for simulation result CSV files using Polars. Returns a presigned URL to download the zstd-compressed JSON summary. For a run whose status is `completed`, `failed` or `terminated` and whose `completedAt` is at least 60 minutes old, and that has no rows for the requested metric (no data file for it, or only a header-only one), the response is 200 with a summary whose `totalRowsProcessed` is 0 and whose projection fields are absent. The one exception is a `completed` run whose only data for the PFC metric is a header-only shard: its `pfc` projection is present with five zero totals (`totalXoffRx`, `totalXoffTx`, `totalXonRx`, `totalXonTx`, `totalTimePausedUsec`) and `byTier` omitted. A run that is not yet settled, or whose status is `invalid`, keeps 404.

parameters.name: sim_id
parameters.description: Simulation ID in sim_xxx format (base32-encoded UUID with prefix)

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: Metric type to summarize. `rank-analysis` is published but returns 501 Not Implemented until its compute path ships. `uet-transport-stats` and `roce-transport-stats` serve `summary`, which carries the whole-run `transport` projection, and `timeSeries`. Both return 501 for `sampled` until that compute path ships.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Output mode (default: summary). `timeSeries` is served for `nd-stats`, `pfc`, `uet-transport-stats` and `roce-transport-stats` and returns 501 Not Implemented for the other metrics; `sampled` is published but returns 501 Not Implemented until its compute path ships. `utilizationBins` (a binned distribution of link utilization over time) is offered for `nd-stats` only: every other metric returns 400 with error code `UNSUPPORTED_COMBINATION`, a permanent answer that must not be retried, and for `nd-stats` the response's `file` presigns a `UtilizationBinsDocument`. `uplinkFairness` (uplink port fairness per switch over time) is offered for `nd-stats` only in the same way: every other metric returns 400 with error code `UNSUPPORTED_COMBINATION`, and for `nd-stats` the response's `file` presigns an `UplinkFairnessDocument`. `completionTimeBins` (a binned distribution of completion times over time) is offered on the Performance projection: `perf` returns the envelope whose presigned URL serves a `CompletionTimeBinsDocument`; `chakra-perf` returns 404 Not Found, as a run with no result shards does, because this shape does not bin its completions; and every other metric returns 400 with error code `UNSUPPORTED_COMBINATION`, a permanent answer that must not be retried.

parameters.name: tier
parameters.description: Tier filter for network device results (default: all)

parameters.name: nodeId
parameters.description: Filter to these node ids. Comma-separated on the wire. An empty list is not accepted — omit the parameter instead.

parameters.name: ifid
parameters.description: Filter to these interface ids. Comma-separated on the wire. An empty list is not accepted — omit the parameter instead.

parameters.name: nicType
parameters.description: Filter to a NIC class.

parameters.name: metricName

parameters.name: application
parameters.description: Filter to these application names. Comma-separated on the wire; values may not contain commas. An empty list is not accepted — omit the parameter instead.

parameters.name: priority

Carries no schema `default`: a schema default makes generated clients send the value on every request, which lists it in X-Ignored-Params on every mode and metric that does not consume it.

parameters.name: tolerance
parameters.description: Dimensionless multiplier on the per-dimension tolerance bands (only consumed when metric=rank-analysis). Omit to get the server default, 0.0. Carries no schema `default`: a schema default makes generated clients send the value on every request, which lists it in X-Ignored-Params on every mode and metric that does not consume it.

parameters.name: outlierThreshold
parameters.description: Outlier deviation-score fraction (only consumed when metric=rank-analysis). Omit to get the server default, 0.10. Carries no schema `default`: a schema default makes generated clients send the value on every request, which lists it in X-Ignored-Params on every mode and metric that does not consume it.

200.description: Summary data with presigned download URL. For a run whose status is `completed`, `failed` or `terminated` and whose `completedAt` is at least 60 minutes old, and that has no rows for the requested metric (no data file for it, or only a header-only one), this is a summary whose `totalRowsProcessed` is 0 and whose projection fields are absent. The one exception is a `completed` run whose only data for the PFC metric is a header-only shard: its `pfc` projection is present with five zero totals (`totalXoffRx`, `totalXoffTx`, `totalXonRx`, `totalXonTx`, `totalTimePausedUsec`) and `byTier` omitted. A run that is not yet settled, or whose status is `invalid`, keeps 404.

X-Ignored-Params.description: Comma-separated, alphabetically ordered list of request params that do not apply to this (mode, metric) pair and were ignored. Absent — never empty — when nothing was ignored.

400.description: Invalid parameters (bad metric, mode, or tier value), with error code `VALIDATION_ERROR`; or, with error code `UNSUPPORTED_COMBINATION`, a result shape the requested projection does not offer (`mode=utilizationBins` or `mode=uplinkFairness` on any metric but `nd-stats`, or `mode=completionTimeBins` on any metric but `perf` and `chakra-perf`). `UNSUPPORTED_COMBINATION` is permanent for the request and must not be retried; its message names the result shape and the projection, and only it carries `X-Ignored-Params`.

X-Ignored-Params.description: Comma-separated, alphabetically ordered list of request params that do not apply to this (mode, metric) pair and were ignored. Sent only with error code `UNSUPPORTED_COMBINATION`. Absent — never empty — when nothing was ignored.

404.description: Simulation not found or no data files available for the specified metric for a simulation that is not yet settled, or is invalid. For `mode=utilizationBins` and `mode=uplinkFairness`, no data files answers 404 whether or not the simulation is settled. For `mode=completionTimeBins`, also a run with no perf result shards, settled or not, and every `metric=chakra-perf` request

413.description: Payload Too Large - The summarized result set exceeds one of the server's size limits: its row count is over the ceiling, summarizing it would exceed the memory budget, or, for `mode=utilizationBins` or `mode=uplinkFairness`, it spans more distinct sample times or more data files than that mode accepts, or, for `mode=uplinkFairness`, its switch uplinks hold more samples than the fold accepts, or, for `mode=completionTimeBins`, it lists more data files than that mode accepts. This condition is permanent for the request and must not be retried.

501.description: The requested mode or metric is recognized but its compute path has not shipped yet

X-Ignored-Params.description: Comma-separated, alphabetically ordered list of request params that do not apply to this (mode, metric) pair and were ignored. Absent — never empty — when nothing was ignored.

503.description: Service Unavailable - Several conditions render this status and they differ in whether a retry resolves them; the ones named here are the known ones rather than a closed set. The common one is a transient fault against the results object store on any mode - a network error, throttling, or a 5xx from the dependency - which is retriable: a client that backs off and retries will usually succeed. A second retriable one is a lost cache-write race the server could not recover from: a concurrent request stored the summary object first, and when this request went back to read it the object was no longer there, so a later attempt normally succeeds against the object the next writer stores. The last is a required backend dependency that is not available or not configured, so the simulation's artifact location could not be resolved. Retrying does not help if the dependency is unconfigured. The response body does not distinguish them, so a client should retry with backoff under a bounded attempt count rather than indefinitely.

504.description: Gateway Timeout - Summary computation exceeded the server's time budget. The request may be retried.

WorkloadMetadata.description: Workload characterization metadata. On a traceset it is returned as stored: the object given at upload, or at the traceset's latest applied promotion that carried metadata. Upload accepts any JSON object and validates only the members UploadWorkloadMetadata describes. Promotion (the Python client's `promote_traceset`) applies its own validation, which this schema does not describe in full. Its member checks read the whole object, the one it is given or else the stored one, through a typed model whose members are spelled in snake_case, so a member that upload stored without checking can make promotion fail; among them, it requires `workload_family` and `workload_name` and checks several members against allowed values. Those checks also read `shape.rank_count` and refuse one that differs from the parallelism product. Separately, its guard against changing the declared rank count reads new metadata as upload does, through camelCase `shape.rankCount` and the parallelism degrees, where a `shape.rank_count` does not count as a declaration; it can refuse new metadata whose declaration is invalid or differs from the count the traceset holds, even when it holds none.

UploadWorkloadMetadata.description: Workload characterization metadata given at upload. This schema describes the members that declare the traceset's rank count, and they are the only members upload validates. Every member is optional, and the object may carry other members, which are stored and returned as given. Upload does not check them, but promotion may refuse them (see WorkloadMetadata).

shape.description: Workload scale. `shape.rankCount` declares the rank count. JSON null counts as absent.

parallelism.description: Parallelism degrees. When at least one of `dp`, `tp`, `sp`, `ep` and `pp` is given, their product declares the rank count. JSON null counts as absent.

WorkloadShape.description: Workload scale. This schema describes `rankCount`; other members of `shape` are stored and returned as given.

rankCount.description: Total rank count: a whole number from 1 to 2,147,483,647. Declaring it alone is enough; parallelism degrees are optional. When parallelism degrees are also given, their product must equal it. JSON null counts as absent.

WorkloadParallelism.description: Parallelism degrees. When at least one of `dp`, `tp`, `sp`, `ep` and `pp` is given, the rank count is their product, with an absent degree counting as 1, and must not exceed 2,147,483,647. Each of those five degrees that is given must be a whole number of at least 1. Each of the five is an independent factor; some training frameworks count an axis differently, for example expert parallelism within data parallelism, and when the rank count is not this product, declare `shape.rankCount` and give degrees only if their product equals it. Other members, such as `cp` and `fsdp`, are not factors; upload stores them as given without checking them, and promotion checks `cp` and `fsdp`. `cp` is the context parallelism degree: the number of ranks that split the attention computation over a long sequence's context. `fsdp` is the fully sharded data parallel (FSDP) degree: the number of data-parallel ranks the model's parameters, gradients and optimizer state are sharded across; it divides `dp` rather than adding ranks. JSON null counts as absent.

dp.description: Data parallelism degree: the number of data-parallel ranks, each processing its own share of the global batch and synchronizing gradients with the others. Without FSDP each holds a full replica of the model; with `fsdp`, each group of `fsdp` of them holds one replica between them, so there are `dp` ÷ `fsdp` replicas.

tp.description: Tensor parallelism degree: the number of ranks that split each layer's weight matrices, and the layer's computation, between them.

sp.description: Sequence parallelism degree: the number of ranks that split each input sequence along its length.

ep.description: Expert parallelism degree: the number of ranks a mixture-of-experts (MoE) model's experts are distributed across, each rank holding a subset of the experts and exchanging tokens with the others.

pp.description: Pipeline parallelism degree: the number of pipeline stages, each a contiguous group of the model's layers on its own ranks, that microbatches pass through in turn.

workloadMetadata.description: Workload characterization metadata: as given at upload, or as given at the traceset's latest applied promotion that carried metadata. Omitted when the traceset has none. Encoded as `oneOf` with explicit `type:'null'` because `nullable:true` adjacent to `$ref` is ignored by the OpenAPI Python generator (the $ref form short-circuits sibling keywords), causing it to emit `WorkloadMetadata.from_dict(value)` without a None guard and crash on JSON null. The `oneOf` form forces the codegen to emit the null branch.

ttlDays.description: Custom TTL in days (1-365). Uses server default if omitted.

workloadMetadata.description: Workload characterization metadata, stored on the traceset as given. It declares the traceset's rank count, which an upload with primary files must declare: either shape.rankCount, or the parallelism degrees parallelism.dp, tp, sp, ep and pp, multiplied together, with an absent degree counting as 1 (cp and fsdp are not factors). When both are given they must be equal. Each value must be a whole number of at least 1. The traceset reports that count as rankCountDerived, and attaching the traceset to a configuration uses it; it cannot be changed after upload. UploadWorkloadMetadata describes the rank-count members; this field accepts any JSON object of at most 65,536 bytes when serialized whose rank-count members are valid, including members UploadWorkloadMetadata does not describe.

name.description: Display name. Display metadata only: inside the simulator the file is always named chakra-mapping.txt.

sizeBytes.description: Length in bytes of the stored object, measured at upload completion.

rankCount.description: Number of Chakra logical ranks the file maps. Derived at upload and stored, so attach validation never re-reads the file.

scaleUpGroupCount.description: Number of scale-up groups the file's second section declares.

MappingFileList.description: One page of mapping files, newest first.

ActiveMappingFileRef.description: The mapping file a configuration or a simulation refers to.

SimpleOperationType.description: MPI collective operation type for simple network simulation workloads.

SimpleAlgorithm.description: Collective expansion algorithm. If omitted, the platform default for the selected operation is used. Names follow MPI/NCCL conventions where applicable. Domain synonyms are accepted on input: rabenseifner → recursiveHalvingDoubling, pairwiseExchange → sequential, pipelinedPairwise → interleaved, flat/linear → direct, recursiveHalving → halving.

SimpleWorkloadPhase.description: A single collective operation phase within a workload. Each phase specifies an operation type, optional algorithm override, and data size.

algorithm.description: Algorithm for this phase. If omitted, the platform default for the operation is used.

dataSize.description: Data size in bytes for this phase.

SimpleWorkload.description: Sequential workload specification. All ranks execute the same ordered phases. Mutually exclusive with groups. Not all algorithms are valid for every operation; see GET /api/v1/simple/compatibility for the full operation/algorithm compatibility matrix including defaults and power-of-two constraints.

ranks.description: Number of participating ranks. Without topologyConstraints, must be one of the reference topology sizes: 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096. Large sizes (8192, 16384, 32768, 65536) require the enable_large_simple_sim_topologies flag. With topologyConstraints, any count the constraint solver can satisfy is accepted; a count above 4096 still requires the enable_large_simple_sim_topologies flag.

phases.description: Ordered list of collective operation phases (1–16). Operations execute sequentially via ctrlDeps chaining.

SimpleGroupSpec.description: Specification for a group of ranks running the same collective operations concurrently with other groups. Multiple groups with the same spec create independent process groups on disjoint rank ranges.

count.description: Number of identical groups to create.

phases.description: Operations each group executes (sequentially within group, parallel across groups).

SimpleSimulationMode.description: Execution mode of a simple simulation. Sequential: all ranks execute the same phases via a single process group. Parallel: ranks are partitioned into independent groups that execute concurrently.

TopologyConstraints.description: Hardware constraints for topology derivation. The solver derives a valid CLOS topology from the specified switch radix and oversubscription ratio. A 2-tier topology is used when ranks fit within the radix capacity (ports × hosts_per_leaf); otherwise a 3-tier pod-based topology (RSW → FSW → SSW) is derived with all switches fully utilized. When present, rank count is not restricted to the reference values — any count satisfying the constraints is valid, and a count above 4096 still requires the enable_large_simple_sim_topologies flag.

switchRadix.description: Switch port configuration for TH5-class (51200 Gbps switching capacity). Format: PortsxSpeed (e.g. 128x400G). 64x800G: 64 ports at 800 Gbps. 128x400G: 128 ports at 400 Gbps (default). 256x200G: 256 ports at 200 Gbps.

subscriptionRatio.description: Target oversubscription ratio (downlink BW : uplink BW) applied at every switch tier. 1:1: equal uplink and downlink bandwidth (default). 2:1, 3:1, and 4:1: more downlink capacity, fewer uplinks. The ratio is applied to both rack switches (RSW) and fabric switches (FSW) in 3-tier topologies. Actual ratios may differ slightly from the target due to integer port rounding.

nicNetworkPortSpeed.description: NIC network port speed in Gbps. Determines the data rate of each host-to-switch connection. When omitted, defaults to the switch link speed from switchRadix (e.g. 400 for 128x400G). The effective link speed between a NIC and its rack switch is min(nicNetworkPortSpeed, switchLinkSpeed) — the lower of the two is used for both topology capacity planning and the generated configuration. PCIe generation is auto-selected to match the effective NIC speed. Allowed values: 50, 100, 200, 400, 800 Gbps.

SimpleSimulationRequest.description: Request to create a simple collective-operation simulation. Exactly one of workload or groups must be specified.

name.description: Optional human-readable name for the simulation. Auto-generated when omitted. SECURITY: this value is interpolated into command strings and Slurm entrypoints executed on cluster nodes, so it is restricted to letters, digits, '-' and '_' (1–255 characters), and must start with a letter or digit (no whitespace, other punctuation, or non-ASCII characters, and no leading '-' or '_').

topology.description: Optional topology reference (reserved for K2 orchestration).

topologyConstraints.description: Hardware constraints for topology derivation. Mutually exclusive with topology.

workload.description: Sequential workload: all ranks execute the same phases. Mutually exclusive with groups.

groups.description: Parallel groups: ranks partitioned into independent groups executing concurrently. Mutually exclusive with workload.

SimpleSimulationStatus.description: Status of a simple simulation submission.

simulationId.description: Unique identifier for the submitted simulation.

workload.description: Resolved workload with algorithms filled in. Present when mode is sequential.

groups.description: Resolved groups with algorithms filled in. Present when mode is parallel.

TopologyTier.description: Switch details for a single tier of the CLOS topology. Tiers are ordered bottom-up: RSW (rack), FSW (fabric), SSW (spine).

name.description: Switch role at this tier. RSW = rack switch (leaf), FSW = fabric switch, SSW = spine switch (super-spine).

switchCount.description: Total number of switches at this tier.

downlinksPerSwitch.description: Number of downlink ports per switch. For RSW: host-facing ports. For FSW: RSW-facing ports. For SSW: FSW-facing ports.

uplinksPerSwitch.description: Number of uplink ports per switch. For RSW: FSW-facing ports. For FSW: SSW-facing ports. 0 for the top-of-tree tier.

downlinkDataRateGbps.description: Data rate on each downlink in Gbps. For RSW downlinks, this is min(nicNetworkPortSpeed, switchLinkSpeed) — the effective host-to-switch speed.

uplinkDataRateGbps.description: Data rate on each uplink in Gbps. 0 for the top-of-tree tier (no uplinks).

effectiveSubscriptionRatio.description: Effective oversubscription ratio at this tier in N:1 notation (e.g., '1:1', '2:1', '1.91:1'), computed from actual port counts and data rates: (downlinks × downlinkRate) / (uplinks × uplinkRate). May differ from the target ratio due to integer port rounding. Null for the top-of-tree tier (no uplinks).

switchCapacityUtilization.description: Percentage of the switch's total switching capacity consumed by connected links at this tier. Computed as (downlinks × downlinkRate + uplinks × uplinkRate) / switchingCapacityGbps × 100. For example, a fully packed 128×400G switch (51200 Gbps) shows 100.0. Under-packed switches or non-standard NIC speeds produce lower values.

TopologyLinks.description: Aggregate link counts at each tier boundary of the topology.

hostToRsw.description: Total host-to-RSW links. Equals totalHosts (one NIC per host).

rswToFsw.description: Total RSW-to-FSW links (RSW count times uplinks per RSW). 0 for 1-tier topologies.

fswToSsw.description: Total FSW-to-SSW links (FSW count times uplinks per FSW). 0 for 1-tier and 2-tier topologies.

ResolvedConstraints.description: The constraint values actually used for topology derivation, including defaults applied when the user omitted a field. For reference topologies (no topologyConstraints in request), shows the equivalent 128x400G / 1:1 defaults.

nicNetworkPortSpeed.description: Configured NIC network port speed in Gbps. This is the value the user requested, or the switch link speed if omitted.

effectiveNicSpeed.description: Effective NIC-to-switch link speed in Gbps: min(nicNetworkPortSpeed, switchLinkSpeed). When the NIC speed exceeds the switch port speed, the link operates at the slower switch speed. This is the data rate used for RSW downlinks and topology capacity planning.

switchLinkSpeed.description: Switch link speed in Gbps, derived from switchRadix (e.g., 400 for 128x400G).

switchingCapacityGbps.description: Total switching capacity per switch in Gbps. All current switch models are 51200 Gbps (TH5-class).

TopologyPreview.description: Derived physical network topology details. Describes the CLOS fabric structure that would be produced for a simulation with the given inputs. This is a pure computation result — no simulation or configuration is created.

tierCount.description: Number of switch tiers. 1 = single rack (RSW only), 2 = leaf-spine (RSW + FSW), 3 = pod-based (RSW + FSW + SSW).

totalHosts.description: Total host count in the topology. Equals total ranks for sequential mode or sum of (count * groupSize) for parallel mode.

ranksPerHost.description: Number of ranks mapped to each host. Currently always 1.

ranksPerRack.description: Number of ranks (hosts) per rack. Equals the RSW downlink count — each host connects to its rack switch via one NIC port.

tiers.description: Per-tier switch details, ordered bottom-up (RSW first, then FSW, then SSW). Array length equals tierCount.

links.description: Aggregate link counts at each tier boundary.

resolvedConstraints.description: The constraint values used for derivation, including defaults applied for omitted fields.

pods.description: Number of pods in the topology. Present only for 3-tier topologies (tierCount = 3).

racksPerPod.description: Number of racks per pod. Present only for 3-tier topologies (tierCount = 3).

spinePlanes.description: Number of independent spine planes. The preprocessor divides SSWs across planes and assigns FSWs round-robin. Present only for 3-tier topologies (tierCount = 3).

TopologyPreviewResponse.description: Response from the topology preview endpoint. Contains the derived physical network topology without creating a simulation or persisting any state.

CompatibilityEntry.description: Compatibility entry for a single MPI collective operation, listing allowed algorithms, the platform default, and which combinations require a power-of-two rank count.

operationType.description: MPI collective operation type this entry describes.

allowedAlgorithms.description: Algorithms valid for this operation type.

defaultAlgorithm.description: Platform default algorithm used when the caller omits the algorithm field.

powerOfTwoRequired.description: Algorithms in this list require the rank count to be a power of two. Empty array if no such constraint exists for this operation.

CompatibilityMatrixResponse.description: The full operation/algorithm compatibility matrix. Each entry describes which algorithms are valid for a given collective operation type, the platform default, and power-of-two constraints.

entries.description: One entry per supported operation type, in enum declaration order.

ChartDefinitionsResponse.description: The chart definitions stored on this platform, served under one schema version

schemaVersion.description: The chart-definition schema version every body in this response conforms to: the version the request named, or chart-definition/v1 when it named none. Each body is the chart's stored body with the highest version not above it. A client refuses the whole document when this is a version it does not parse.

definitions.description: The stored definition bodies, verbatim and ordered by id. There is no per-element wrapper: each body carries its own top-level id.

items.description: One stored chart-definition body, served as-is. The server interprets only its top-level id and reads nothing else in it for meaning. The absence of a type is deliberate — a described type-less schema is what the Rust generators carry through as a raw JSON value — so this description is required and must not be removed.
